In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
there is no clear evidence for a deconfinement phase transition for light flavors and charmonia.
the screening masses are not significantly modified by the presence of a finite temperature.
there is no evidence for a deconfining phase transition in the charmonium spectrum.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the light quark and the charmonium systems show different behaviors at high temperature.
the light mesons and the charmonia are not completely screened even in the high temperature phase of QCD.
the screening masses for the light mesons and the charmonia do not change significantly at temperatures less than 420 MeV, which is the temperature of the chiral crossover.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the screening masses are not a good measure of the binding energies and hence the masses of the hadrons in the deconfined medium.
the chiral symmetry restoration and the charmonium dissociation are two distinct phenomena.
the chiral crossover transition in the light quark system is a rather smooth crossover and not a phase transition in the sense of the first order phase transition.
